study type: Retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional quality of life assessment, comparing EA patients to healthy controls.
exposure: presence of associated VACTERL-H anomalies (vertebral, anorectal, cardiac, renal, limb anomalies and/or hydrocephalus)
cohort: The study included 66 patients (40 aged 2-7 years, 26 aged 8-17 years) who underwent surgery for esophageal atresia between 2004 and 2020, alongside a comparison group of 43 healthy children.
finding: Quality of life in EA patients was significantly influenced by anatomical EA type, repair mode, low birth weight, tracheomalacia, frequent lung infections, presence of associated VACTERL-H anomalies, gastrostomy placement, and other surgical interventions, with older EA patients (8-17 years) demonstrating significantly higher emotional scale quality of life than healthy controls.
mod_finding: Repair mode was identified as a significant factor influencing patients' quality of life.
followup_time: Up to 17 years post-birth/surgery (patients aged 2-17 years at assessment)
cross-section timing: Quality of life questionnaires were administered to patients aged 2-17 years at the time of the study, identified from a cohort operated between 2004 and 2020.
birth_weight: Not specified for the overall cohort, but low birth weight was identified as a significant risk factor for quality of life.
gest_age: Not specified for the overall cohort, but gestational age was investigated and found not to significantly impact quality of life.
